description: Phase 6q gate — string concatenation `||`. New token CONCAT (two consecutive `|`). New opcode `Concat { left_reg, right_reg, dest }`. New precedence level `concat` between `unary` and `multiplicative`. NULL propagates; Integer coerces to decimal TEXT; Real raises VDBE_UNSUPPORTED_CAST (deferred to 6r). All phase1..6p fixtures must stay green.

cases.name: concat-left-associative-three
cases.description: `a || b || c` parses as `(a || b) || c` (left-assoc). Observable as the order of result assembly, but all standard concat implementations produce the same string.

cases.name: concat-integer-integer
cases.description: Both operands Integer → both coerced to decimal text, result is Text.

cases.name: concat-negative-integer
cases.description: Unary `-` binds tighter than `||` (precedence: unary > concat).

cases.name: concat-i64-min-via-expression
cases.description: Integer coercion of i64::MIN. Unary minus cannot directly produce -9223372036854775808 because +9223372036854775808 is out-of-range for i64; construct via (0 - MAX - 1) or similar.

cases.name: concat-null-in-chain
cases.description: NULL propagates through any position in a chain.

cases.name: concat-real-left-rejected
cases.description: Phase 6r lifted the Real-operand UNSUPPORTED_CAST in Concat; Real is now coerced to fixed 17-digit scientific notation. Fixture retained under its original name to pin the post-6r behavior.

cases.name: concat-real-right-rejected
cases.description: Phase 6r lifted the Real-operand UNSUPPORTED_CAST in Concat.

cases.name: concat-real-both-rejected
cases.description: Phase 6r lifted the Real-operand UNSUPPORTED_CAST in Concat.

cases.name: concat-null-short-circuits-over-real
cases.description: NULL short-circuits BEFORE the Real-rejection check. `NULL || 3.14` → Null, NOT an error.

program.sql: CREATE TABLE people (first TEXT, last TEXT);
CREATE TABLE t (id INTEGER, name TEXT);
SELECT id FROM t WHERE name || '!' = 'foo!';

cases.name: concat-with-null-column
cases.description: A NULL column value propagates through `||`, yielding Null for that row.

program.sql: CREATE TABLE t (a TEXT, b TEXT);

cases.name: concat-result-is-text-not-integer
cases.description: `1 || 2` must evaluate to Text('12'), verifiable by piping through LENGTH (two UTF-8 bytes → Integer 2). If the result were Integer 12, LENGTH would raise VDBE_TYPE_MISMATCH.

cases.name: concat-precedence-vs-comparison
cases.description: `||` is higher precedence than comparison. `'a' || 'b' = 'ab'` parses as `('a' || 'b') = 'ab'` → true (1).

cases.name: concat-precedence-vs-additive
cases.description: `||` is higher than `+ -`. `2 + 3 || 4` parses as `2 + (3 || 4)` = Integer(2) + Text('34') → EVAL_TYPE_ERROR on the `+` operator (same error name + field shape as phase2c1 `SELECT 1-'x';`). If concat were lower precedence, it would parse as `(2 + 3) || 4` = '54' (no error). Asserting the error distinguishes the two precedence assignments. Uses EVAL_TYPE_ERROR (not VDBE_TYPE_MISMATCH) because the canonical error for binary-operator type mismatches is EVAL_TYPE_ERROR {op, left_type, right_type}; VDBE_TYPE_MISMATCH is reserved for scalar-function / aggregate type errors.

cases.name: concat-with-parens
cases.description: Parentheses override precedence; `(a || b)` is a primary expression.

cases.name: concat-bare-pipe-lex-error
cases.description: A single `|` (not followed by another `|`) raises LEX_UNEXPECTED_CHARACTER at the `|`'s position.

cases.name: concat-prefix-not-allowed
cases.description: `||` has no unary / prefix form; appears at expression-start → parse error at the CONCAT token.

program.sql: CREATE TABLE t (a TEXT, b TEXT);
SELECT b FROM t ORDER BY a || b;

cases.name: concat-with-cast-integer
cases.description: CAST coerces Real to Integer first, then Integer || Text works.
